title: Fabrication and Characterization of Griffithsin-modified Fiber Scaffolds for Prevention of Sexually Transmitted Infections
protocol: Weigh 720 mg of 50:50 poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA; 0.55 to 0.75 dL/g, 31-57 kDa) into a 10 mL scintillation vial.
Add 3.0 mL HFIP to the glass scintillation vial containing PLGA using a serological glass pipette.
Cover the vial with plastic film.
Measure and record the vial mass.
Incubate the polymer suspension overnight at 37 °C.
Monitor the vial mass during incubation; if mass decreases due to solvent evaporation, add HFIP to restore original mass.
Prepare the electrospinning apparatus.
Aspirate the polymer solution into a 3 mL syringe.
Connect a blunt 18-gauge, ½ inch needle tip to the syringe and dispense excess solution to remove headspace in the needle tip.
Place the syringe on a syringe pump and set the flow rate to 2.0 mL/h.
Connect the power source to the syringe needle.
Electrospin the polymer solution using a voltage of +27 kV; maintain a distance of approximately 25 cm between the needle and collector.
Use a fume hood or an enclosed apparatus during electrospinning due to solvent vapor production.
Turn off the power source once the entire solution is electrospun.
Allow the mandrel to spin for an additional 30 min after turning off the power source.
Turn off the rotating mandrel collector.
Use a razor blade to cut the fiber from the mandrel.
Gently peel the fiber from the mandrel using the blade.
Collect the electrospun PLGA fiber into a labeled Petri dish.
Place the collected fibers in a desiccator overnight to remove residual solvent.
Prepare solutions of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and MES buffer.
Dissolve 8 g NaCl, 0.2 g KCl, 1.44 g Na2HPO4, and 0.24 g KH2PO4 in 1 L of ultrapure water to prepare PBS.
Dissolve 19.52 g MES (free acid) and 29.22 g NaCl in 1 L of ultrapure water to prepare MES buffer.
Ensure the final pH of each solution is between 7.2 - 7.5 for PBS and 5.0 - 6.0 for MES buffer using a pH meter.
Prepare individual working solutions of EDC (2 mM) and NHS (5 mM).
Remove EDC and NHS from the freezer to equilibrate to room temperature before weighing.
Weigh 4 mg of EDC into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Weigh 6 mg of NHS into another microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1 mL MES buffer to each tube containing EDC and NHS.
Vortex both tubes vigorously to ensure the reagents are fully dissolved.
Prepare a solution of hydroxylamine by weighing 70 mg into a 50 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Add 20 mL PBS to the hydroxylamine and vortex to dissolve.
Mass out an appropriate amount of PLGA fiber into a 15 mL conical centrifuge tube, typically 75 mg per reaction batch.
Add 8 mL of MES buffer to the 15 mL tube containing the PLGA fiber.
Add 1 mL of EDC solution to the tube.
Add 1 mL of NHS solution to the tube.
Close and seal the 15 mL tube with plastic film.
Place the tube on a rotator for 15 min at room temperature.
Quench the reaction by adding 14 µL of β-mercaptoethanol to the tube.
Invert the tube several times to ensure complete mixing.
Discard the supernatant from the tube.
Rinse the PLGA fiber twice with 10 mL of PBS.
Add an appropriate amount of GRFT stock solution to the tube.
Add enough PBS to bring the final volume to 8 mL.
Close and invert the tube to ensure thorough mixing.
Seal the tube with plastic film.
Place the tube on a rotor for 2 h.
Quench the reaction by adding 2 mL of hydroxylamine solution into the 15 mL centrifuge tube after a 2 h incubation.
Mix the quenched solution well and discard the supernatant.
Rinse the surface-modified PLGA fiber twice with ultrapure water to remove unconjugated GRFT.
Transfer the rinsed fiber to a Petri dish and place it inside of a desiccator until dry.
Store the dried fiber in a Petri dish at 4 °C.
Place a strip of double-sided carbon tape on an SEM specimen mount.
Label the bottom of the specimen mount with sample identifying information using a permanent marker.
Cut three samples from one surface-modified fiber and place them on separate specimen mounts.
Sputter coat the samples for 90 s, at 2.4 kV.
Image the coated samples at 8 kV with magnification ranging from 1,000 to 5,000X.
Mass out 2 mg of fiber in triplicate into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Add 1 mL dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) to the tube and vortex.
Incubate for 1 min at room temperature to dissolve the fiber completely.
Dilute a 10 μL aliquot of the DMSO-fiber solution from step 4.2 in Tris-EDTA buffer (TE) by at least 100-fold.
Store diluted samples at -20°C until loading characterization with ELISA.
Weigh 5 - 10 mg of surface-modified fiber and place it in a microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1 mL of an appropriate solution that mimics the physiological environment to each sample.
Incubate the samples for 1 h on a rotating shaker at 200 rpm, 37°C.
Remove approximately 1 mL of TE buffer containing the desorbed GRFT from the vial after incubation.
Aliquot the removed buffer and store it at -20°C until protein quantification.
Transfer the sample to a new microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1 mL of fresh buffer solution to the fiber within the microcentrifuge tube.
Incubate for the next time point, with typical time points including: 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 24, 48, 72 h, and 1 wk.
Coat a 96-well ELISA plate with 0.1 mL of HA (10 μg/mL) per well as previously described.
Seal the coated plate with plastic film.
Incubate the sealed plate overnight at 4°C.
Remove the coating buffer from each well.
Add 0.3 mL of blocking buffer to each well and incubate for at least 2 hours at room temperature.
Rinse the plate 3 times with PBS-P (1x PBS with 0.1% polysorbate 20).
Dispense 0.1 mL of sample, standard, or negative control into respective wells.
Incubate the plate again for 1 hour at room temperature.
Rinse the plate 3 times again with PBS-P.
Add 0.1 mL of primary antibody diluted 1:10,000 in PBS to each well and incubate for at least 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash the plate 3 times with PBS-P.
Add 0.1 mL of secondary antibody diluted 1:10,000 in PBS to each well and incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash the plate 3 times.
Add 0.1 mL of TMB substrate to each well.
Monitor color development for approximately 2 minutes.
Add 0.1 mL of H2SO4 (1 N) to quench the reaction.
Read the absorbance at 450 nm on a microplate reader.
Average background OD values from wells that only received PBS and subtract this value from experimental group readings.
